regime_context: US market shows AI Infrastructure as the clear leader (eligible, rank 1, breadth 0.71) with Cybersecurity as a crowded challenger and a narrowing rotation (19/49 eligible). Gate_helps is true, so trend discipline has historically cut drawdown here, but cross-sectional rank carries no forward alpha; the macro backdrop is unscheduled/geopolitics-heavy (0.75 surprise share), which argues for humility.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Cybersecurity can convert its challenger status into a confirmed leadership handoff from AI Infrastructure: AI Infra's durability_bar (0.68) is fading while Cybersecurity's is 0.85 with full breadth — I am watching for CIBR to close the rotation margin (0.342) to under 0.10 against AI Infra's SMH while both remain gate-eligible; the watch retires if the margin widens back above 0.50 instead.

theses.subject: AI Infrastructure
theses.thesis: The leading theme passes the absolute-trend eligibility gate with broad participation (breadth 0.71) and is not crowded (z 0.59). Its challenger margin is comfortable (0.34). While the rank itself is not a return forecast, the trend-gate leg is the one validated risk control in this market's history, so a disciplined continuation lean on the gate-eligible leader is defensible — this is a staying-power read, not a momentum chase.
evidence: crowding_z: 0.59, crowded: false (no sizing cap flag)
durability_bar: 0.68 (mixed but above the headline's own bar)
theses.dissent: AI Infrastructure has a 'fading' val_state on the headline and only a mixed hurst tag, meaning the trend is not cleanly persistent — if the macro surprise share (0.75) resolves risk-off, the broad leader is exactly where crowded-in capital exits.

falsifier.text: SMH lags SPY by 5% or more cumulative over any 10-day window before the 30-day check

theses.subject: Cybersecurity
theses.thesis: Cybersecurity is the strongest-gated theme in the whole book: durability_bar 0.85 (top decile), breadth 1.0 (total participation), and a clean 'trend' hurst tag. It is the challenger to AI Infra. However it is crowded (z 1.8) — this is a sizing caution, not a fade per guardrails, so the lean is a modest continuation, not an aggressive add.
theses.dissent: Crowding z of 1.8 is the single most extended position in the eligible set — attention spikes in thematic ETFs historically mark tops, so the very strength of the flock into CIBR is the bear case for near-term chop.

falsifier.text: CIBR breadth drops below 0.5 while still eligible before the 21-day check

theses.subject: US Energy Complex
theses.thesis: Energy is one of only three eligible themes with a clean 'trend' hurst tag in the top ten, is gate-eligible with healthy breadth (0.727), and is not crowded (z 0.83). It offers a non-tech, non-AI diversifier at a moment when the macro narrative is dominated by geopolitics (3 of 12 recent macro themes) — plausibly supportive of energy names. This is a trend-gate continuation, not a geopolitical prediction.
evidence: macro_narrative: geopolitics n=3 among dominant themes
theses.dissent: Energy is a reflexive asset to geopolitical headlines, and with 75% of macro narrative being unscheduled surprises, a rapid de-escalation could unwind the energy bid as fast as it built.

falsifier.text: XLE loses gate eligibility (eligibility flips to false) before the 30-day check

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
